subject: mathematics
question_text: If tan20° = λ, then show that (tan160° − tan110°)/(1 + tan160° · tan110°) = (1 − λ²)/(2λ).

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Express both tangents in λ
steps.margin_note: First mark. 160° reduces to −tan20° = −λ; 110° is 90° + 20°, which gives −cot20° = −1/λ. Both are now in λ.

recall.must_convey: That tan160° = −λ and tan110° = −1/λ, both written in terms of λ.
accept: tan one sixty is minus lambda and tan one ten is minus one over lambda
reduce both to lambda, one gives minus lambda and the other minus cot which is minus one by lambda
express both tangents in terms of lambda
tan one sixty minus lambda, tan one ten minus one by lambda

steps.why: tan(90° + θ) gives a COTANGENT, not a tangent — which is why one of the two comes out as a reciprocal. Missing that leaves the expression unsolvable.
common_mistakes: Losing a minus sign on either reduction.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The denominator becomes 1 + 1 = 2, and the numerator combines over λ — giving the required form directly.
steps.memory_tip: The denominator becomes 1 + 1 = 2, and the numerator combines over λ.

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives (1/λ − λ)/2, which combines to (1 − λ²)/(2λ).
accept: substitute to get one over lambda minus lambda all over two which is one minus lambda squared over two lambda
the denominator becomes two and the numerator combines over lambda
simplify to one minus lambda squared over two lambda
substitute cheste one minus lambda square by two lambda vasthundi
the answer is one minus lambda squared over two lambda

steps.why: The product of the two tangents is (−λ)(−1/λ) = 1 exactly, which is what makes the denominator a clean 2.
common_mistakes: Failing to combine the numerator over a common denominator.

insider_note: tan110° reduces through 90° + 20°, so it becomes −cot20° = −1/λ, NOT −tan20°. That reciprocal is what produces the λ² in the answer.
